preamble: Backing of the voiced dental fricative [ð] to the voiced velar fricative [ɣ] is a defining change of late Gaelic: Old Irish non-initial and lenited d was [ð], but between the 13th and 18th centuries the dental fricatives were lost across the Goidelic languages, broad [ð] merging with lenited g as [ɣ]. Scottish Gaelic keeps the result word-finally: Old Irish mod /ˈmoð/ 'manner' > modh /mɔɣ/, clad /ˈklað/ 'ditch, bank' > cladh /kʰl̪ˠɤɣ/ 'churchyard'.

examples.note: Non-initial Old Irish d was the fricative [ð]; the broad fricative is now velar, spelled dh like gh.
Irish cladh /klˠai/ has instead vocalized the fricative.

sources: Wiktionary contributors (2026). cladh (Scottish Gaelic, Irish). https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/cladh
